adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — same PUT/DELETE verb mismatch as above; a real production PUT to /admin/groups/1/members resolves to add_members, never remove_member, so this test proves nothing about the shipped routing.

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the admin groups member routes are defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`, so a PUT to `/admin/groups/:group_id/members` will route to `add_members`, not `remove_member`. However, the diff shows the spec starting a `.remove_member` context and using `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, ...`, which mismatches the shipped routing/HTTP verb (it should be `:delete`). This means the test is not exercising the real routed endpoint semantics and could pass while the routed behavior differs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:94,103,115,125 — new `.add_members`/`.remove_member` specs call controller actions directly with hand-picked group_id/user_id params, never exercising config/routes.rb's real route recognition end-to-end.

adjudication.rationale: The cited specs use standard Rails controller-spec style (e.g., `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: ...`) to exercise the controller actions and their parameter handling. It’s true they don’t verify routing end-to-end against `config/routes.rb`, but that is not a correctness/bug/security defect introduced by the diff—it's simply a choice of test scope. Nothing in the diff indicates the routes are misconfigured in a way that these specs would mask as a real failure, and controller tests are still valid for these actions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40-60 and admin-group.js.es6:51-65 — `removeMember`/`addMembers` promise chains have no rejection handler (unlike save/destroy which use bootbox.alert); a 422 from can_not_modify_automatic or any network error is silently swallowed with no UI feedback.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `Discourse.Group#addMembers` and `#removeMember` both return `Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` with no `.catch`/rejection handler. The controller actions `addMembers` and `removeMember` simply call these methods (and in `removeMember` even ignore the returned promise inside the bootbox callback), providing no UI error handling. If the server responds with 422 (e.g., `can_not_modify_automatic`) or there is a network/API error, nothing in these code paths shows an alert or otherwise informs the user—unlike the `save` flow which wires up a failure handler and displays feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65-82 — `usernames.split(",").each { User.find_by_username }` is one query per submitted username (N+1) with no cap on list size or payload length.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members (new in the diff), the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username| if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end end`. This performs one DB lookup per submitted username, which is an N+1 query pattern relative to the input size. The method also accepts the raw `usernames` string from params and iterates over all entries without any explicit cap on how many usernames can be supplied (beyond whatever web server/framework request-size limits exist, which are not in this diff). This is a real, verifiable performance/DoS-risk issue introduced/present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19-36 — `members` response shape changed from a bare array to `{members, meta}`; a breaking, unversioned API contract change for any external consumer not covered by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the response changed from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare serialized array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`. That is a concrete, backwards-incompatible change in the JSON shape returned by the public `/groups/:group_id/members` endpoint (now also always paginated with default `limit=50`, whereas previously non-automatic groups returned all members). The diff updates the Ember client to consume `result.members`/`result.meta`, but any other consumer expecting an array would break, and there is no versioning or compatibility shim shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65-75 — unbounded comma-separated usernames list drives unlimited sequential `User.find_by_username` lookups in one admin request; no max-count guard (self-DoS/resource exhaustion).

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` reads `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` with a `User.find_by_username(username)` inside the loop. There is no guard on the number of usernames processed (nor on total string length beyond whatever the web server/framework enforces), so a single request can trigger an arbitrarily large number of sequential DB lookups and group membership operations. This is directly verifiable from the added code and matches the proposed finding (a potential self-DoS/resource exhaustion vector, even if limited to admin access).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34-47 — `update` only guards `name` against automatic groups (`!group.automatic`); `alias_level` and `visible` can still be silently mutated on protected/system automatic groups (admins, moderators, trust_level_*) via a 200 response.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the diff intentionally allows `visible` (and `alias_level`) to be updated even for automatic groups, while only preventing renaming (`group.name` guarded by `!group.automatic`). This is validated by the newly added spec (`context ".update"`) which updates an automatic group (id: 1) with `visible: "true"` and asserts `group.visible` becomes `true` while the name does not change. Therefore, the behavior described is not a defect introduced by the diff; it is explicitly desired/covered by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19-36 — `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is attacker-controlled with no upper bound on a route reachable by any user passing `ensure_can_see!`; unbounded serialization amplification vector (widened from base, which only bounded automatic groups).

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes the behavior to always apply `limit`/`offset` and returns a JSON payload containing `members: serialize_data(members, ...)`. The new `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is entirely client-controlled and is passed directly into `group.users...limit(limit)` with no upper bound. Since this route is reachable by any user who can pass `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`, a requester can supply an arbitrarily large `limit` to force a large DB read and large JSON serialization/response, which is a plausible amplification/DoS vector. The diff does not introduce any server-side cap to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` with params moved from nested `params[:group][:visible]` to top-level; a stale cached client still POSTing the old nested shape during a rolling deploy gets `visible` silently forced to false with a 200 success response.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the server-side parameter contract for group create/update from nested params[:group][:visible] (and other fields) to top-level params[:visible]/params[:name] (Admin::GroupsController#create and #update). There is no fallback to read the old nested shape. If an older/cached client still submits { group: { visible: "true" } }, then params[:visible] will be nil and `params[:visible] == "true"` evaluates false, causing `group.visible` to be set to false while the request can still succeed (200) because it’s a valid value. This is a concrete backward-compatibility regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19-36 — bare-array → `{members, meta}` response shape break is a hard failure (`result.map is not a function`) for any external/API client not updated in this diff, during the deploy window.

adjudication.rationale: Real: the diff changes `GroupsController#members` from returning a bare serialized array (`render_serialized(members.to_a, ...)`) to returning an object `{ members: ..., meta: ... }`. Any existing client code (including older cached frontend JS or external consumers) that expects the old array shape and does `result.map(...)` will now receive an object and fail at runtime (`result.map is not a function`). The diff updates *some* internal callers (`Discourse.Group.findMembers`) to use `result.members`, but it does not preserve backward compatibility at the endpoint level, so un-updated clients would hard-break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — default limit=50 now applied to ALL groups (base only paginated automatic groups); non-automatic groups >50 members are now silently truncated on the public member-list template, which has no pagination controls.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff removes the special-casing that only paginated automatic groups and now always applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, returning only `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` plus meta. On the client, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now requests `/groups/:name/members.json` with `limit`/`offset` and stores the returned `members` array on the group model. The public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` was changed from iterating `model` to iterating `members`, i.e., it will render only the limited page returned by `findMembers`. Unlike the admin template, the public `group/members.hbs` diff shows no added pagination controls, so groups with >50 members will display only the first 50 by default without any UI to navigate further. This is a concrete behavior change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb create/update — `usernames` param dropped entirely from create/update; any external caller or stale client still submitting `usernames` to bulk-set membership gets a silent 200 with the field ignored.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#create and #update to no longer read membership from a `usernames` parameter. Previously, `create` read `params[:group][:usernames]` and `update_put` applied `payload[:usernames]` to `group.usernames`. Now `create` only uses `params[:name]`/`params[:visible]` and `update` only uses `params[:alias_level]`/`params[:visible]`/`params[:name]` (when not automatic). Membership changes are moved to new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints. As a result, a caller that still sends `usernames` alongside valid top-level update attributes (or even just sends `usernames` on update) will get a successful response while the membership intent is ignored (update calls `group.save` and returns success_json even if only ignored params were provided). This is a real behavioral/API-compatibility break introduced by the diff; it can be silent for update and for create if `name` is provided in the new expected place.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js `asJSON` — `usernames` key removed from the payload; "assign members at group-creation time" is silently retired with no task doc, commit body, or spec noting the deliberate narrowing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `usernames` from `Discourse.Group#asJSON` and replaces `createWithUsernames/saveWithUsernames` with `create/save`, shifting membership changes to new endpoints (`Admin::GroupsController#add_members` / `#remove_member`) and a separate UI action (`addMembers`). This is a deliberate behavior change (no longer adding members in the same POST/PUT as group creation/update), and the specs are updated accordingly (the old create-with-usernames test is removed; new tests cover create stripping spaces and add_members separately). The proposed finding frames this as a defect due to being "silently retired" with no spec noting it, but the change is reflected in both code and tests and is not inherently incorrect/buggy within the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:24-30 — add-members UI is gated behind `{{#if id}}`, making it unreachable during group creation; membership-add is redefined from a create-time to an edit-only feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does gate the members list and the “Add members” UI behind `{{#if id}}` in `admin/templates/group.hbs`, so it will not appear for a new, unsaved group (no `id`). However, this matches the model/controller/API changes in the same diff: group creation no longer accepts usernames (`createWithUsernames` removed; server `create` ignores membership), and membership changes are now done via separate `/admin/groups/:id/members` endpoints which require an existing group `id`. So while this is a behavioral change (you can’t add members at creation time anymore), it’s not a clear bug/defect within the diff—it’s an intentional redesign to make membership edit-only after the group exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb create/update — `usernames` param removed from both actions, eliminating the old "replace full membership list in one call" semantics in favor of additive/singular-only endpoints, with no documented sign-off that this semantic narrowing was intended.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `usernames` handling from `Admin::GroupsController#create` and `#update`, but it simultaneously introduces explicit membership endpoints (`add_members`, `remove_member`) with matching routes (`PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`) and updates the JS model/controller to use `group.addMembers(...)` and `group.removeMember(...)` instead of `saveWithUsernames/createWithUsernames`. The UI template also only shows the “add members” widget once the group has an `id`, consistent with a deliberate two-step flow (create group, then add members). Since the diff consistently updates callers and tests to this new API, the only critique is about undocumented intent / semantic narrowing for external clients, which is not a verifiable defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb — removed test "is able to create a group" (which asserted `usernames` set at create) with no replacement assertion anywhere for create-time membership.

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally changes group creation semantics: `Admin::GroupsController#create` no longer accepts `params[:group][:usernames]` (or any `usernames`) and the Ember model/controller also switches from `createWithUsernames(usernames)` to `create()` with membership managed via the new `add_members` endpoint (`PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members.json`). The UI only exposes the member-adder once `id` exists. Therefore the removed spec that asserted create-time membership matches the new behavior; the absence of a replacement assertion is a test-coverage change, not a verifiable correctness defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19-35 — no spec file exists anywhere for the public `GroupsController`; the new pagination/limit/offset/total contract is completely untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to return a new JSON shape with pagination meta, and the only spec file touched/added is `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`. However, the finding’s claim that “no spec file exists anywhere for the public GroupsController” is not verifiable from this diff alone (it could exist outside the shown changes). Also, “untested” is a test-coverage concern rather than a concrete defect introduced in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb — old tests "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users" and "succeeds silently when removing non-members" were deleted and never reintroduced for the new add_members/remove_member actions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the old incremental PATCH update specs, including the two cases about adding non-existent users and removing non-members, and the new specs added for `add_members`/`remove_member` do not reintroduce equivalent coverage. However, this is a test coverage regression rather than a verifiable functional/correctness defect in the code itself (the new controller code still silently ignores unknown usernames and `users.delete` is typically idempotent). So the finding doesn’t identify a concrete bug introduced by the diff, only missing tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — `offset = params[:offset].to_i` has no test for negative or out-of-range offsets; unclamped value passed straight to ActiveRecord `.offset`.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes pagination to apply for all groups and sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` without clamping/validating it. A request can supply a negative offset (e.g., `offset=-10`), which will be passed directly to `group.users...offset(offset)`. ActiveRecord will emit SQL with a negative OFFSET, which can error on some DBs (e.g., PostgreSQL rejects negative OFFSET) and cause a 500. The client-side code clamps offset, but the controller still accepts arbitrary params, and there are no tests covering negative/out-of-range offsets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — no test covers duplicate usernames (e.g. "bob,bob") or an empty/whitespace-only usernames string.

However, the proposed finding is specifically about *test coverage* (no test for "bob,bob" or empty/whitespace-only usernames), not about a concrete, verifiable defect introduced by this diff. The diff does not establish that duplicates would create incorrect state (there may be DB uniqueness constraints or `group.add` may be idempotent), nor that empty/whitespace usernames must error; as written they would simply result in no users added and still return success. Therefore this is not a clearly verifiable problem in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec .add_members context — no test passes a username that fails to resolve to a User, so a regression in the silent-skip-unknown-username behavior would go undetected.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, the previous controller spec suite explicitly tested that adding a non-existent username succeeds silently (in the removed incremental PATCH tests: `it "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users" ...`). The new `.add_members` spec context only tests (1) automatic group rejection and (2) adding valid users; it contains no case where `User.find_by_username` returns nil. Since `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` now silently skips unknown usernames (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`), the intended “silent-skip-unknown-username” behavior is unverified by tests after this change, so a regression would indeed go undetected.

That’s a test-coverage suggestion, not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff. In Rails, `has_many :through`/HABTM association `delete` is typically a no-op when the record isn’t associated, so the lack of an explicit test for that behavior isn’t evidence of a bug in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:8 — `ilike` → `ILIKE` casing rename is unrelated to membership semantics, adds noise to an otherwise substantive file.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the SQL operator from `ilike` to `ILIKE` in `Admin::GroupsController#index` (`groups.where("name ilike ?", ...)` → `groups.where("name ILIKE ?", ...)`). In PostgreSQL this operator is case-insensitive and both casings are functionally equivalent, so this does not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect. At most it is a minor style/consistency change (“noise”), which the instructions explicitly exclude from being a REAL problem.
